guarantees.claim: For each i, a prim_alert_sender is instantiated with IsFatal set to 1'b1 and AsyncOn set to AlertAsyncOn[i].
The instance's alert_tx_o output is connected to the top-level alert_tx_o[i] signal.
The instance's inputs are connected: alert_req_i to alerts[i], alert_test_i to alert_test[i], alert_rx_i to alert_rx_i[i], clk_i and rst_ni to the system clock and reset.

formal.consequent: u_prim_alert_sender.alert_req_i == alerts[i] && u_prim_alert_sender.alert_test_i == alert_test[i] && u_prim_alert_sender.alert_rx_i == alert_rx_i[i]

formal_sketch.consequent: u_prim_alert_sender.alert_req_i == alerts[i] && u_prim_alert_sender.alert_test_i == alert_test[i] && u_prim_alert_sender.alert_rx_i == alert_rx_i[i]

assumptions.claim: The clock (clk_i) and active-low reset (rst_ni) must be properly provided and the reset must be asserted before operation to initialize the alert sender instances correctly.
assumptions.risk: If reset is not properly applied, the alert sender may fail to initialize, causing missed or spurious alerts.

formal_sketch.consequent: The clock (clk_i) and active-low reset (rst_ni) must be properly provided and the reset must be asserted before operation to initialize the alert sender instances correctly

assumptions.claim: If AlertAsyncOn[i] is asserted (1), the connected alert_rx_i[i] and alert_tx_o[i] must be properly synchronized or designed for asynchronous operation; otherwise (0) they are synchronous to clk_i.
assumptions.risk: Metastability from unsynchronized asynchronous signals could cause unreliable alert signaling.

formal_sketch.consequent: the connected alert_rx_i[i] and alert_tx_o[i] must be properly synchronized or designed for asynchronous operation; otherwise (0) they are synchronous to clk_i

uncertain_points.claim: The alert_ack_o and alert_state_o outputs of the prim_alert_sender are left unconnected. If the sender requires an acknowledgment to deassert the alert, this could cause the alert to remain asserted indefinitely.
uncertain_points.risk: Fatal alert may persist, leading to system lockup or inability to recover.

formal_sketch.consequent: The alert_ack_o and alert_state_o outputs of the prim_alert_sender are left unconnected. If the sender requires an acknowledgment to deassert the alert, this could cause the alert to remain asserted indefinitely

uncertain_points.claim: All alert senders are configured with IsFatal=1'b1. If any of the alerts are intended to be non-fatal, this could cause unnecessary fatal escalations.
uncertain_points.risk: Over-escalation may force a system reset or shutdown for recoverable errors, impacting availability.

security_implications: This chunk configures all DMA alert senders as fatal (IsFatal=1) and leaves the alert acknowledgment (alert_ack_o) and state (alert_state_o) unconnected. Any alert triggered by DMA (e.g., error conditions) will result in an unrecoverable fatal escalation, yet the local logic gives no feedback or clearing mechanism. The lack of acknowledgment could cause the alert to remain asserted, potentially locking the alert handler and the system, leading to denial of service or an inability to recover from an error state. Additionally, if any alert is intended to be non-fatal, the hardcoded fatal nature would over-escalate, unnecessarily triggering system-wide resets or shutdowns.
